title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: One read per file, and it is a correctness rule
summary: The removal edit read every file twice, computing offsets on one read and applying them to another. Between the two, a file can change.

highlights.title: Ranges and text from the same bytes
highlights.description: Offsets measured on a first read were written against a second one. A file that changes between two awaits put the deletion somewhere else.

highlights.title: Thirty dead symbols, one read
highlights.description: A file reached by many stale imports was read once per import. The read is memoized for the whole edit now.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: The text of a file is read once per removal edit, so the ranges and the text they apply to cannot diverge.
A file named by several stale imports is no longer read once per import.
